# Fixture corpus

Small test files, one per parsing or signal pathology.
Make sure to keep the list of examples updates according to the supported methods to extract time-series data.

| File | Pathology |
|---|---|
| `arm_multi_device.csv` | CSV with an `id` column and unit-suffixed axis names (`tcp_pose_x_mm`, `tcp_pose_y_mm`, `tcp_pose_z_mm`) that resolve to `proprio.ee_pose` in `dictionary.yaml`. Rows are sorted by `t_ms` first and `id` second — as in the real recordings this fixture is modelled on, entities interleave (t0 -> every entity sampled at t0, t1 -> every entity sampled at t1, ...) rather than being grouped by id. Four entities (`armA`–`armD`) share timestamps — 50 of the 96 distinct `t_ms` values have more than one entity on them, up to 4 at once — so entity splitting is exercised rather than assumed. Each entity also carries a signal pathology: `armA` is regularly sampled at 10 ms and is the negative control; `armB` has a flatlined `tcp_pose_z_mm` channel (constant 75.0 for every sample); `armC` has a burst of 5 consecutive dropped samples (indices 20–24 of its own 50-sample grid); `armD` has a jittery clock — its `t_ms` wobbles around the nominal 10 ms grid by up to a few ms per sample instead of landing on it. |
| `imu_stream.txt` | JSONL inside a `.txt` file — the real container is not what the extension claims. One record per line, `{"t_us": ..., "acc": [x, y, z], "gyro": [x, y, z]}`; nested arrays that should expand into `acc[x,y,z]` and `gyro[x,y,z]` channel groups by index. Regular 200 Hz microsecond-epoch timestamps. |
| `pose_log.txt` | Whitespace-delimited with the column names inside a comment line (`# timestamp ax ay az`) rather than a header row. Regular 50 Hz, float-seconds timestamps starting at `0.0`. |
| `capture_index.json` | A dict keyed by strings that carry a source, a hash and a timestamp (`AUTOLab+5d05c5aa+2023-07-07-10h-00m-34s`), each key one timestamped record. Nested one level deeper by camera serial (`CAM7F3A`, `CAM9B21`) — a second entity dimension. Gaps between keys are irregular (3–9 s), so rate-based metrics do not apply. |
| `video_meta.json` | Flat single-record JSON metadata blob (`fps`, `codec`, `duration_sec`). No time index, so this file must be skipped with a reason — it is the corpus's only no-timeseries fixture. |
| `lerobot_v3_tiny/` | A directory-shaped LeRobot v3.0 dataset — the corpus's only fixture an adapter bids on as a whole subtree rather than one file at a time. Two episodes (8 and 6 frames) share one data parquet, split by `episode_index`, and one mp4 per the single declared camera (`observation.images.up`), so one episode spans three files at once. `meta/info.json` declares `fps: 30` and `robot_type: "so100_follower"`, read rather than inferred. `observation.state` carries six SO-101 motor names that resolve to nothing in `dictionary.yaml` and lands `unmapped.observation.state`; `observation.velocity` resolves to `proprio.joint_velocity` by its own key. |
| `lerobot_v2_0_tiny/` | A directory-shaped LeRobot v2.0 dataset with a per-episode layout: two episodes (8 and 6 frames), each its own data parquet and its own mp4 for the single declared camera (`observation.images.up`), both in `chunk-000` since `chunks_size: 1000` never rolls over. `meta/info.json` declares `fps: 30` and `robot_type: "so100_follower"`; `meta/stats.json` (rather than `meta/episodes_stats.jsonl`) is what marks this tree v2.0 rather than v2.1, though the adapter reads neither. `observation.state` carries six SO-101 motor names that resolve to nothing in `dictionary.yaml` and lands `unmapped.observation.state`; `observation.velocity` resolves to `proprio.joint_velocity` by its own key. |
| `lerobot_v2_1_tiny/` | A directory-shaped LeRobot v2.1 dataset proving chunk rollover and a camera-less tree: two episodes (5 and 4 frames) at `chunks_size: 1`, so episode 0 lands in `chunk-000` and episode 1 in `chunk-001`, and no video feature at all. `meta/info.json` declares `fps: 30` and `robot_type: "so100_follower"`; `meta/episodes_stats.jsonl` (rather than `meta/stats.json`) is what marks this tree v2.1 rather than v2.0. Feature resolution is the same: `observation.state` lands `unmapped.observation.state`, `observation.velocity` resolves to `proprio.joint_velocity`. |
| `hdf5_tiny.hdf5` | A single-file HDF5 dataset whose episode boundaries live in its group structure rather than in any column — two sibling groups under `runs` (`session_a`/`session_b`, 5 and 4 samples), found structurally rather than by name. `runs.attrs["fps"]` declares `20.0`, read rather than inferred. Each episode group carries `actions` (width 4) and `rewards` (scalar) directly, resolving through `dictionary.yaml`, plus a `signals/` subgroup one level down holding `eef_pose` (resolves to `proprio.ee_pose`) and `probe_raw` (unmapped) — so the one-level-of-nesting read is exercised by the fixture itself. |
| `mcap_tiny.mcap` | A single-file MCAP recording with three ROS 2 topics, each on its own clock. `/joint_states` (`sensor_msgs/msg/JointState`) carries a `std_msgs/Header` whose `stamp` sits half a millisecond before the record's own `log_time`, so it resolves to `proprio.joint_position` by message type and keeps `Clock.CAPTURE`, with `position_*`/`velocity_*`/`effort_*` channels and its string `name` array skipped. `/cmd_vel` (`geometry_msgs/msg/Twist`) carries no header, lands on `Clock.LOG`, and resolves to `action.base_velocity_command` by its topic name rather than its message type; its nested `linear`/`angular` vectors flatten to six dotted axis channels. `/camera/wrist/image_raw` (`sensor_msgs/msg/Image`) is a blob-payload topic — timestamps and no channels at all — and resolves to nothing, landing `unmapped./camera/wrist/image_raw`. |

Generated by `uv run python scripts/generate_fixtures.py`. Fixtures are
committed data: the generator does not run before pytest, and rerunning it
is a manual step outside the test suite.
